name: Dr. Agarwals Health Care Ltd
title: Dr. Agarwals Health Care Ltd - 544350 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Analyst / Investor Meet - Outcome

read.thesis: Q1 FY27 revenue up 26% to INR614 crore with 15.5% surgery volume growth and ~8% realisation uplift; 18 greenfield launches, but 60-facility FY27 plan now needs 30 in H2 and ~INR20 crore greenfield losses weigh on margins.

triggers.quote: Q1 has set the base, 18 facilities launched, out of which 16 surgical, a record for any single quarter in the history of this company.

triggers.label: H2 launches 30 vs 12 in Q2
triggers.quote: we're looking at adding 12 facilities for Q2 and 30 in the second half.

triggers.label: Mature cohort SSSG 16.3%
triggers.quote: recording a strong 16.3% year -on-year growth and accounting for 75.9% of the overall group revenues.

Overall, the green plot is around close to INR20 crores at corporate EBITDA level.

summary.headline: Dr. Agarwal's Q1 FY27 revenue from operations rose 26% YoY to INR614 crores, with Ind AS EBITDA of INR177 crores (28.5% margin) and PAT margin of 8.9%.
summary.overview: Q1 FY27 was a record quarter with 18 greenfield facilities launched (16 surgical), the highest ever in one quarter, and total income of INR620 crores up 24% YoY. Revenue from operations grew 8.8% QoQ, and Ind AS EBITDA rose 25.2% YoY to INR177 crores with margin up 30 bps to 28.5%. PAT margin expanded 127 bps to 8.9% despite greenfield losses of about INR20 crores at corporate EBITDA level. Same-store growth for facilities pre-FY23 was 16.3%, driven by roughly 8% volume and 8% value growth.

financial_highlights.change: +26% YoY; +8.8% QoQ; vs INR487 crores in Q1 FY26
from INR24.7 crores in Q1 FY26; interest on deferred acquisition payable down to INR3.6 crores from INR6.8 crores

financial_highlights.metric: Share of PAT attributable to owners

segments.name: Surgical services
segments.commentary: Contributed 66% of group revenue; about 91,000 surgeries in the quarter, up 15.5% YoY. Cataract surgeries were about 74% of surgeries and grew 16.5% YoY; refractive about 4.4%.

segments.name: South region
segments.commentary: INR387 crores revenue (63% of group), up 22.8% YoY; 189 facilities, 7 added in the quarter; only 65% of surgical facilities fully mature.

segments.name: West region
segments.commentary: INR91 crores revenue (15% of group), up 24% YoY; 52 facilities, including 5 new greenfield launches.

segments.name: North region
segments.commentary: INR57 crores revenue (9% of group), up 50.5% YoY; 30 facilities including 6 new; Delhi NCR now has 8 facilities.

segments.name: East region
segments.commentary: INR16 crores revenue, up 21% YoY; 14 facilities; new leadership team in Kolkata.

segments.name: Facility vintage
segments.commentary: Pre-FY23 facilities INR465 crores (75.9% of revenue) growing 16.3%; FY24 vintage INR48 crores (+19.6%); FY25 vintage INR62 crores (+38.6%); FY26 vintage INR33 crores. Emerging facilities are 21% of revenue.

guidance_outlook: FY27 plan of 60 new facilities including 40 surgical centres; 18 launched in Q1, with 12 planned for Q2 and 30 in H2.
30+ signed LOIs in place for the greenfield pipeline; management says it remains confident in the full-year plan.
Three to five more Delhi NCR facilities planned for the rest of FY27.
Management expects to sustain growth through deeper micro-market penetration, new geographies and adoption of advanced procedures.
Merger expected to close around mid-November 2026, per an individual investor's question.
Management called 12-13% SSSG a phenomenal outcome; it expects South SSSG to be similar to the 16.5% seen in the cohort up to FY26, but did not commit to sustaining it.
capex_capacity: 18 greenfield facilities launched in Q1 FY27, including one large tertiary facility in Thane and 15 secondary facilities; 2 primary facilities in J&K and Tamil Nadu.
Network now 285 facilities across 14 states and 5 UTs, covering 165 cities; 31% Tier 1, 63% other markets, 6% international.
Since FY23, 166 greenfield facilities added; additions rose from 10 in FY23 to 18 in Q1 FY27 alone.
Management says it is working to raise the launch pace, citing compliance requirements for properties in the pipeline.
Doctor count of 1,057, up about 23%, mostly from new centres; about 100 doctors added in the last four months.
demand_pricing: Premiumisation contributed about 7.5% to value growth and price hikes about 0.5% so far this year, so roughly 8% like-to-like value growth. Volume growth was about 15-16%.
Average realisation per cataract rose from INR28,000-30,000 four years ago to about INR42,000 now, driven by premium lenses and femto cataract adoption.

Femto cataract procedures were 1,548 (+33.4% YoY); SMILE refractive procedures +36.2% YoY; retinal procedures 3,861 (+30% YoY); high-end cataract share 29.3% of 67,000 cataract surgeries. Femto additional charge is about INR35,000 against a licence fee of about INR10,500-11,000.
Payer mix: 63.6% cash, 27.7% insurance and TPA, 8.6% government schemes.
Senior doctor attrition is 2-3%; group-wide attrition is 16-17%, mainly junior doctors.

qa_highlights.question: How much of revenue growth came from volume versus value (case mix and price)?
qa_highlights.answer: COO Rahul Agarwal said premiumisation was about 7.5% and price hikes about 0.5%, so value growth was close to 8% like-to-like against volume growth of about 15-16%.

qa_highlights.question: What are the losses from new facilities?
qa_highlights.answer: Rahul Agarwal put greenfield losses at about INR20 crores at corporate EBITDA level, including FY26 and FY27 centres and pre-operating losses.

qa_highlights.question: What were the finance cost and lease interest figures?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Yashwanth Venkat said about INR25 crores was paid on acquisition liabilities in Q1 and lease interest was about INR18 crores. Finance cost fell to INR23.5 crores from INR24.7 crores.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the 16% SSSG for pre-FY23 facilities, and how much was footfall?
qa_highlights.answer: Rahul Agarwal said SSSG split into about 8% volume and 8% value; OPD growth of 6% plus 2% from conversion drove the value growth.

qa_highlights.question: Will realisation keep rising about 10% a year?
qa_highlights.answer: Adil Agarwal said the direction is up with insurance and premium lens adoption, but he could not commit to the exact pace of around 10% or 8%.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins fall as femto technology costs rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Adil Agarwal said rupee gross margin will rise because the femto add-on (about INR35,000) exceeds the licence fee (about INR10,500-11,000).

qa_highlights.question: Why is the launch pace constrained, and can it be raised?
qa_highlights.answer: Adil Agarwal said management is working to increase the pace, citing compliance requirements; Q1's 18 launches set the benchmark.

risks_watch: Greenfield losses of about INR20 crores per quarter at corporate EBITDA level; 30 launches are planned in H2 versus 12 in Q2, which is back-loaded.
Delhi NCR and North growth is partly base effect from Operation Sindoor and floods; Delhi facilities are far from maturity.
Group-wide doctor attrition of 16-17%, though senior doctor attrition is only 2-3%.
Pricing growth depends on premiumisation; price hikes were only about 0.5% so far this year.
Merger completion expected around mid-November 2026; the closing timeline was given in a single answer.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on volumes, South/North growth and the greenfield pipeline. Management was guarded on forward SSSG and realisation pace, declining to commit to a specific percentage.
key_quotes: This new fiscal year commenced with record-breaking results.
We are working on improving the launch pace. I think we have set that benchmark by this quarter.

growth.why: Management reiterated a 60-facility FY27 addition plan (18 launched in Q1, 12 in Q2, 30 in H2) backed by 30+ signed LOIs, with same-store growth of 16.3% in pre-FY23 facilities and about 8% like-to-like value growth; revenue grew 26% YoY in Q1 but no FY27 revenue growth figure was guided.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Ind AS EBITDA margin rose 30 bps to 28.5% and PAT margin expanded 127 bps to 8.9% despite about INR20 crores of greenfield losses, with rupee gross margin rising as femto add-on (about INR35,000) exceeds licence fee (about INR10,500-11,000).

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: 18 facilities launched in Q1 FY27, 12 planned for Q2 and 30 in H2, backed by 30+ signed LOIs, bringing the FY27 plan to 60 facilities including 40 surgical centres.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Volume grew about 15-16% YoY in Q1 and pre-FY23 same-store volume rose about 8%, with surgeries up 15.5% to about 91,000 and new facilities ramping.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex is not discussed directly, but the 60-facility FY27 build-out and 3-5 more Delhi NCR facilities imply continued investment; no capex amount or utilisation figure was given.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management was confident on the pipeline but declined to commit to forward SSSG or realisation pace, and no revenue or margin guidance was raised.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: The 30 H2 launches are back-loaded versus 12 in Q2, and greenfield losses of about INR20 crores per quarter could weigh on margins if the launch pace slips.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Femto cataract procedures rose 33.4% to 1,548 and SMILE rose 36.2%, with premium lens and advanced procedure adoption cited as growth drivers, though no specific new product launch was named.

rows.label: Realisation per cataract rising
rows.why: Average cataract realisation rose from INR28,000-30,000 four years ago to about INR42,000, but price hikes were only about 0.5% this year and management would not commit to a pace of around 10% or 8%.

rows.label: Merger completion
rows.why: Management indicated the merger is expected to close around mid-November 2026, and a finance cost decline was already visible with acquisition-payable interest down to INR3.6 crores from INR6.8 crores.

rows.label: Greenfield LOI pipeline
rows.why: 30+ signed LOIs back the greenfield pipeline, and management remains confident in the full-year plan of 60 facilities.

tone.note: Management was confident on volumes, South and North growth and the greenfield pipeline, but guarded on forward SSSG and realisation pace; analysts pressed on volume versus value split, greenfield losses, realisation trajectory and femto margin impact.
